chunks: And indeed, one of you will surely lag behind; if a calamity should befall you, he will say: 'God was gracious to me that I was not among them as a witness.'

key_terms.قَدْ أَنْعَمَ اللَّهُ: God has shown favor / been gracious
key_terms.لَيُبَطِّئَنَّ: will surely lag behind / hold back

ai.seo_question: Who is the person that lags behind in the Quran and what does he say after a defeat?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often interpreted as describing the hypocrite (munafiq) who lags behind in battle, with some scholars linking it specifically to Abdullah ibn Ubayy or the general archetype of those who avoid jihad. When a setback occurs, he claims divine favor for his absence, using this rationalization to justify his cowardice and lack of commitment to the community. This highlights the psychological mechanism of hypocrisy, where failure is reframed as a blessing to preserve one's ego.
